extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in natural theology / skeptics of design arguments
extracted.subtask_description: Assembling and presenting observational, natural-history style proofs (eyes, fish, seas, earth, plants, tides, etc.) as evidence for a wise Creator; a sequence of concrete examples used to persuade skeptics. Focuses on empirical phenomena used as premises in natural theology/design arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of fishes to water
rubrics_metrics.description: The Structure of the Eyes of Fiſhes differ from that of the Land Creatures, the first being adapted only to ſee in Water, the other in the Air. Let him alſo conſider the Shape and Form of Fiſhes, where he will plainly diſcover all thoſe Qualities that are requiſite to ſupport them in Water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anatomical and functional differences (eyes, body shape, salt vs. fresh-water species, reproductive abundance) as direct evidence of purposive design — i.e., point to specific morphological features matched to environments and note the mutual relations between fishes and waters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual relation of fishes and waters
rubrics_metrics.description: If he deſires to be further informed of the Relation which the Fiſhes and Water have mutually to one another; ... compare it with this Diſſertation about the Sea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize mutual dependencies (habitat, physiology, life cycles) as a criterion: show how organisms and their medium form complementary systems that imply governance rather than chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulation of waters prevents land overflowing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circulation of the Waters does likewiſe Preſerve the Land from overflowing. ... such an innumerable Company of Rivers ... do Day and Night continually diſcharge into the Sea ... and yet not fill the Sea, nor force it to exceed its Bounds, and overflow the Land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the hydrologic cycle (evaporation, vapour rising, condensation on mountains, rains forming brooks and rivers) as an explanatory mechanism that prevents catastrophic accumulation; treat the existence of such a regulated cycle as evidence of a ruling intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrostatics / dykes demonstration (Holland)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dykes or Banks of Holland: take notice in how many Places the Waters of the Zuider-Sea, are higher than the Lands that lie within the ſaid Dykes. ... Would he not consider it as a continual and unconceivable Miracle, that thoſe Dykes, ſo {mall and ſlender in refpe& to the Waters that preſs upon them, have not long ſince been overturned ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the apparent paradox (vast sea vs. slender dykes) plus basic hydrostatic principles (depth not breadth increases pressure; a small column of water behind a dyke can balance a large surface) to argue that the sea obeys laws and arrangements that prevent catastrophe — presented as evidence of governance. Include the sketch/figurative explanation (ABCD, AC, BD, etc.) as supportive demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sea’s self-limiting production of sand
rubrics_metrics.description: Shew any one, that has ſeen a ſtormy ſea ... a handful of Sand, tell him, that ſo ſmall ... can reſtrain the Rage of ſuch watry Mountains; ... that the Sea itſelf does, according to all probability, produce that Sand, and thereby becomes itſelf a Bridle to its own fearful Powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that the production of sand by evaporation/sea-processes (citing experiments by Hooke and Platt) and sandbanks placed along coasts function as natural bulwarks — interpret such self-regulating features as signs of design rather than blind chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coastal defenses: sandbanks, seaweed, shoal profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Can he obſerve the double Sand-banks placed along the Coaſts, which are like Walls and Bulwarks againſt the Incurſion of this all-deſtroying Sea-Enemy? Can he obſerve the oblique Aſcent of the Shoar, in order to break the Force of the Sea, or the Heighth of the Downs that lie behind, without being obliged to own, that a Great and Adorable Engineer has vouchſafed thereby to fortune this Country againſt an Invader ...?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to multiple coastal features (sandbanks, seaweed used in dykes, shoal angles that dissipate wave energy) and their protective roles; treat their regular occurrence and utility as evidence of providential arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel/strait moderates sea’s force
rubrics_metrics.description: Forasmuch as ... the Promontary of France, and that Great and Noble Ifland of Britain makes between em a Streight or Channel ... which is broad enough for a Fleet of Ships to pass thro', and yet narrow enough to hinder this dreadful Ocean ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geographic configurations (English Channel) and tidal observations (height differences at Calais vs North Sea) to argue that large-scale features act to moderate oceanic forces — presented as further proof of ordered design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tides: ebbing and flowing as ordered phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caſe of Ebbing and Flowing: ... the Waters of the Sea, under the Moon ' or thereabouts, do on either ſide of the Globe raiſe an exceeding great and convex Mountain, which daily ſurrounds the Earth. ... these Motions ... seem to be kept among the inſcrutable Secrets of the Creator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat tidal phenomena (lunar influence, raised 'mountain' of water) and their regularity as complex ordered motions that preserve navigational utility and contribute to the maintenance of marine conditions — therefore indicating design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow and ebb preserve marine life and water purity
rubrics_metrics.description: No, whether the Great Ruler does not wiſe make uſe of thoſe Motions and ... the Waves, 'to- preſerve the Sea-Water from corruption, even to the very Bottom of them, to keep the Fiſhes and other Creatures alive, and the N it ſelf pure and ſweet ... we leave to the ſudgmenrofuhi Learned: At leaſt tis well enough known, how very uſeful the Flowing and Ebbing of the Sea is to Mariners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that regular currents and tidal mixing prevent stagnation and corruption, supporting life and navigation; present usefulness to mariners as experiential confirmation of beneficial order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term preservation of water quantities and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Water beſtowed in - ſuch great abundance, and for ſo many Ages gratis, to Living Creatures. ... we are taught by daily Experience, that the Waters of the Sea, of Rivers, and of Rains, have remain'd always Unchanged ; and preſerv'd their Nature and Properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out the empirical puzzle that despite continuous mechanical, chemical, and biological use, water has retained its properties over ages — use this constancy (and balance between losses and gains) to infer governance rather than fortuitous replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earth produces grass, corn, and variety of plants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Earth produces Graſs, Corn, &c. ... that the firſt grows of its own accord out of the Earth in ſuch an infinite Number of Places, and ſerves for Proviſion to the Cattle. ... the Earth is adapted to produce Corn and other Things, which ſerve Mankind for Food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ubiquity and productivity of basic plant foods (grass for cattle, cereals for humans) as evidence of apt disposition of earth to support large numbers of creatures; emphasize ease of production of fodder vs. labor required for human food to show purposeful arrangement (and even moral lesson about labour/curse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beasts as converters of inedible grass into food for humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Beaſts are Kitchens for the Graſs ... Oxen, Sheep and all other Creatures ... are taken by Men for Food, as ſo many living and walking Kitchens; in which is prepared the otherwiſe unprofitable Graſs, and becomes good, wholſome and palatable Food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue functional roles in ecological chains: show how animals render otherwise inedible plant matter into human-edible products (meat, milk) as a contrivance that implies design and mutual suitability among species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of productions from one earth as sign of wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: From one and the ſame Earth, [God] is able to produce ſuch an unconceivable variety of Plants. ... from the Aptitude and Property which this Earth has to produce ſo great a Diverſity of Plants, an irrefragable Proof may be drawn, that he who invented and compounded ſuch a Mixture, muſt have had ... particular knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the multiplicity of useful products (herbs, medicines, fruits, building timber, dyes, etc.) arising from the same underlying matter as evidence of intelligent composition and provisioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earth’s fertility is durable and renewable
rubrics_metrics.description: Earth is never conſumed, nor becomes entirely barren. ... whereas so much Earth has been made uſe of ... yet in so great a Series of Time it has never failed, nor entirely loſt its Fecundity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical and agricultural observation (land can be renewed by fallowing, turning, rain/air effects, nitrous salts) to show mechanisms that restore fertility, and interpret those restorative processes as part of a provident system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms of restoring soil fertility (air, rain, tillage)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Experiment to ſhew, that the Air makes the Earth Fruitful. ... the barren plot, lying Fallow for a Year, and having been frequently broke into ſmall Pieces, cauſed the Seed ... to grow very thick and ſtrong, without uſing Dung or any thing elſe to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite concrete agricultural practice and simple experiments (fallowing, turning, exposure to air and rain) as observable mechanisms by which fertility is renewed — useful on the evidentiary side of the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of universal loathsomeness by circulation of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: All the Meat with which they are fed, is converted in their Bowels to a loathſome Dung and Excrement. ... Add hereto, that ſo many Millions of Men and Beaſts ... would have rendered the whole Earth and the Air exceeding nauſeous and loathſome ... This Loathſomeneſs prevented ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to the large-scale problem (accumulation of waste, corpses, dung) and then show how natural cycles (decomposition, incorporation into soil, growth of new plants) avert catastrophe; interpret such circulation as intelligent provision preventing otherwise inevitable disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulation of living things: earth→life→earth repeatably
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circulation of almoſt all living: Earth to Earth; ... Can it be then thought that ſuch ingeniously contrived Bodies of Men, of Beaſts, and of Plants, proceed all from the Earth, without the Concurrence of a great Director? ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the systemic fact that organisms are formed from earth-derived matter and return to earth on death — a continual revolution sustaining life — as strong cumulative evidence for a directing intelligence; emphasize difficulty of replicating such a system by human design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural corroboration of natural observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Texts of Scripture proving the same, and Convictions from the Whole. ... The Wiſdom of the Almighty in his Holy Word has often plainly occur'd to me, in which this unconceivable Circulation of Things, from Earth to Earth again, is mention'd with great Energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing natural-theological arguments, complement empirical examples with reference to scriptural passages that reflect the same order and cycles; present scripture as supportive corroboration for readers already receptive to it.
